title: Pokrovsky--Talapov and Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless Phase Transitions in Bilayer Superconducting Films under an In-Plane Magnetic Field
abstract: We study finite-temperature phase transitions in a Josephson-coupled bilayer superconducting film with compact layer phases under an in-plane magnetic field. At zero temperature, where thermally excited layer vortices are absent, the relative-phase sector undergoes a Pokrovsky--Talapov (PT) commensurate--incommensurate (C--IC) transition from a commensurate Fulde--Ferrell (C/FF) state to an incommensurate Bloch superconducting (IC/Bloch SC) state. At finite temperature, compactness separates two distinct defect mechanisms. The C--IC boundary remains a PT soliton-entry line: interlayer Josephson vortex--antivortex-pair solitons enter with the square-root onset $ρ_{\rm sol}\propto [k_0-k_0^c(T)]^{1/2}$. Thermal melting is instead Berezinskii--Kosterlitz--Thouless (BKT)-like, with correlation exponent $η=1/4$ at the boundary, but the active vortex channel changes across the phase diagram. Josephson locking suppresses elementary layer vortices in the C/FF state and selects a same-vorticity layer-pair BKT channel, whereas elementary layer vortices control melting of the IC/Bloch SC state.
summary: This paper theoretically maps the complex finite-temperature phase diagram of a Josephson-coupled superconducting bilayer under an in-plane magnetic field. It distinguishes between two types of transitions: the Pokrovsky–Talapov transition driven by soliton entry, and Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless melting governed by vortex unbinding. The analysis uses advanced RG techniques to characterize these competing critical lines.
main_problem: The study investigates finite-temperature phase transitions (Pokrovsky–Talapov and Berezinskii–Kosterlitz–Thouless) in a Josephson-coupled bilayer superconducting film subjected to an in-plane magnetic field.
main_result: The phase diagram is characterized by three distinct boundaries: the PT soliton-entry line separating C/FF from IC/Bloch SC, and two BKT-like thermal melting lines (C–L and IC–L).
method: The authors employ Renormalization Group (RG) analysis on a continuum action derived from the Ginzburg-Landau functional, supplemented by Monte Carlo simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a Josephson-coupled superconducting bilayer ($\psi_1, \psi_2$) placed in an in-plane magnetic field ($H$). The effective theory involves phase dynamics governed by relative and common phase sectors.
key_observables: Correlation exponents (expected to approach 1/4 at BKT transitions), helicity moduli ($\Upsilon$), and the soliton density $ho_{	ext{sol}}$ determining the C–IC boundary.
important_parameters: In-plane magnetic field parameter $k_0 = 2\pi H a / \Phi_0$, temperature $T$, and Josephson coupling strength $K$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on weak-fugacity RG schemes and assumes that the C–IC transition is governed by soliton entry, distinct from thermal vortex unbinding.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing the coexistence of PT (soliton) and BKT (thermal melting) boundaries, and show finite-size scaling diagnostics confirming the expected critical exponents for the thermal transitions.
paper_structure: The paper develops an effective continuum action, applies RG techniques to track vortex fugacities and stiffnesses, determines the zero-temperature PT boundary via fixed-sector free energy crossings, and analyzes the finite-temperature BKT boundaries using correlation function decay and helicity modulus criteria.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding how competing topological defects (solitons vs. vortices) dictate phase transitions in superconducting systems, which has parallels with critical phenomena studied in quantum many-body physics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Phase diagrams of the compact layer-phase model. (a) Representative (k0, T) cut at K = 0.2. Symbols mark Monte Carlo thermal-boundary diagnostics and fixed-soliton-sector C–IC crossings; curves are inferred phase boundaries. (b) Three- dimensional (k0, T, K) phase diagram, showing the PT C–IC wall and the BKT-like C–L and IC–L melting surfaces.

FIG. 2. Bilayer model and representative current patterns. (a) Two superconducting layers separated by a, coupled by Josephson tunneling g, and subject to an in-plane field H = H ˆy, indicated by ⊗. (b) Fulde–Ferrell state with uniform superfluid density, counterpropagating intralayer supercurrents, and zero interlayer Josephson current JT = 0. (c) Bloch SC state with modulated superfluid density; blue arrows show in-plane supercurrents, and colored loops mark interlayer Josephson vortex–antivortex unit cells.

FIG. 3. Fixed-soliton-sector test of the PT soliton-entry boundary at K = 0.2. Points are thermodynamic-integration crossings for L = 64, 100, 128 and T = 0.35, 0.45, 0.55, plotted as kN versus ρ2 N+1/2. Linear fits to kN = kc 0(T)+A(T)ρ2 N+1/2 over 0.002 ≤ρ2 N+1/2 ≤0.008 give the finite-temperature C– IC boundary.

FIG. 4. Phase-correlation diagnostics for thermal melting at K = 0.2, L = 100. (a) C–L cut at k0 = 0.25; (b) IC–L cut at k0 = 1.5. Symbols show fitted correlation exponents from C11, C12, C21, C22. Guides mark η = 1/4 and the stiff- ness criteria Υ+ = T/(2π) in (a) and Υ+ + Υ−= 2T/π in (b). The small spread among the Tη estimates from different Cαβ channels and their small offset from TΥ are finite-size ef- fects expected to vanish in the thermodynamic limit; the C–L finite-size trend is shown in Appendix .
